pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Tulsi leaves are offered to which gods? (1 mark)
   A. Lord Shiva only
   B. Guru Nanak
   C. Lord Mahavir
   D. Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna

2. The Beas river is linked with which region of India? (1 mark)
   A. Kerala
   B. Gujarat
   C. Punjab
   D. Bengal

3. Which of these is a use of water at home? (1 mark)
   A. Making rocks
   B. Making the wind blow
   C. Cooking food
   D. Producing sunlight

4. How would you practise Ahimsa at school? (1 mark)
   A. By teasing the smaller children
   B. By not bullying and by caring for animals
   C. By hurting insects
   D. By breaking things

5. Narsimha is an Avtar of which god? (1 mark)
   A. Lord Shiva
   B. Lord Buddha
   C. Lord Vishnu
   D. Lord Ganesh

6. What is the holy scripture of the Sikhs? (1 mark)
   A. Kalpasutra
   B. Dhammapada
   C. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
   D. Ramayan

7. Whom did Ram marry in the Bal Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Ganga
   B. Sita
   C. Saraswati
   D. Kaikeyi

8. Which quality of Ram is taught in the Bal Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Laziness
   B. Cruelty
   C. Pride
   D. Respect for parents and teachers

9. Which of these were sons of King Dasharatha? (1 mark)
   A. Ram, Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughna
   B. Ram, Sigala, Bharat and Shibi
   C. Lakshman, Devadatta, Ram and Bharat
   D. Prahlad, Ram and Jetha

10. How should you receive prasad? (1 mark)
   A. With your right hand or both hands, and say thank you
   B. With your left hand only
   C. By snatching
   D. By refusing rudely

11. How can you show a Mandir in a drawing? (1 mark)
   A. A circle only
   B. A river
   C. A zigzag line
   D. A rectangle hall with a pointed spire

12. On which festival do many students pray to Saraswati? (1 mark)
   A. Paryushan
   B. Vasant Panchami
   C. Madaraka Day
   D. Maha Shivratri

13. What does pita mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Wealth
   B. Father
   C. Mother
   D. Friend

14. How should you dress to visit a Mandir? (1 mark)
   A. Wearing a heavy coat
   B. Modestly
   C. Very informally
   D. Wearing school uniform

15. What does the white colour of Saraswati stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Purity and peace
   B. Hunger
   C. Heat
   D. Anger

16. What did the Buddha say about a person's words? (1 mark)
   A. They should be true, kind and helpful
   B. They should be false
   C. They should be rude
   D. They should be loud

17. The shopkeeper gives you Ksh 100 in change but you should get Ksh 70. What is the extra amount? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 30
   B. Ksh 100
   C. Ksh 70
   D. Ksh 170

18. When getting off a vehicle, what should you do first? (1 mark)
   A. Stand and push
   B. Run
   C. Wait for it to stop
   D. Jump

19. How does the breath in happen in Kapaal Bhaati? (1 mark)
   A. By humming
   B. By hand
   C. By itself
   D. By force

20. Where should the hands be in Vajra Asana? (1 mark)
   A. In the air
   B. On the thighs
   C. Behind the head
   D. On the floor in front

21. Every living being has what, according to Hindu belief? (1 mark)
   A. A temple
   B. A festival
   C. A scripture
   D. An atma, a small part of the divine

22. Which of these is a good way to pray? (1 mark)
   A. Say thank you and ask for wisdom and kindness
   B. Ask only for gifts
   C. Shout
   D. Sit and laugh

23. What is Madaraka Day? (1 mark)
   A. A Jain festival
   B. A Hindu festival
   C. A sports day
   D. A Kenyan national holiday on 1 June

24. Which festival is a national festival? (1 mark)
   A. Paryushan Parva
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. Maha Shivratri
   D. Vasant Panchami

25. Which activity is suggested to learn about festivals? (1 mark)
   A. Write a composition on your favourite festival
   B. Read a book quietly
   C. Copy a friend's essay
   D. Watch television all day

26. Which festival comes first in the year in the lesson's timeline? (1 mark)
   A. Maha Shivratri
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. Paryushan
   D. Jamhuri Day

27. Which prayer is chanted on Maha Shivratri? (1 mark)
   A. Om Namah Shivaya
   B. Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   C. Micchami Dukkadam
   D. Ik Onkar

28. Which is the first month listed in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Magha
   B. Phalguna
   C. Chaitra
   D. Kartika

29. The Indian traditional calendar is based on what? (1 mark)
   A. The school year
   B. The Moon and the Sun
   C. Only the stars of the south
   D. Only the rain

30. What is a calendar? (1 mark)
   A. A prayer
   B. A kind of map
   C. A way of counting days, weeks and months
   D. A festival

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write the meaning of Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva. (3 marks)

32. Name two sacred rivers mentioned in the lesson. (2 marks)

33. Explain the meaning of the word Paramatma. (2 marks)

34. Describe how to make a decorated calendar. (4 marks)

35. Which festival in the lesson is a national holiday and why? (2 marks)

36. Describe what Prince Siddhartha did when a swan was hurt. (3 marks)

37. Explain the Sikh idea of Kirat Karni. (2 marks)

38. Give three benefits of yoga. (3 marks)

39. Give four roles of sacred plants. (4 marks)

40. Write the Indian names for Thursday and Friday. (2 marks)

41. Choose one scripture and explain how a child can apply its teaching at home and at school. (5 marks)

42. Give the meaning of Maha Shivratri. (2 marks)

43. Give three activities to learn about temples. (3 marks)

44. A shopper gives you Ksh 500 and you buy items for Ksh 320. Work out the change and say what to do if you are given Ksh 200 by mistake. (4 marks)

45. Describe the snake story of Lord Parshvanath. (3 marks)

46. Explain why the time and place of the defeat of Hiranyakashipu are special in the story. (3 marks)

47. Why is water sometimes used in worship? Give three points. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna
   Tulsi leaves are offered to Vishnu and Krishna.

2. C — Punjab
   The Beas flows in Punjab, where Sikhism began.

3. C — Cooking food
   We use water for cooking, drinking and washing.

4. B — By not bullying and by caring for animals
   Ahimsa means not harming others.

5. C — Lord Vishnu
   Narsimha is one of Lord Vishnu's Avtars.

6. C — Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
   Sikhs follow it as their eternal Guru.

7. B — Sita
   Ram married Sita in Mithila.

8. D — Respect for parents and teachers
   Ram was truthful, polite and brave.

9. A — Ram, Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughna
   These were the four brothers.

10. A — With your right hand or both hands, and say thank you
   Receive with politeness.

11. D — A rectangle hall with a pointed spire
   A hall with a spire is a simple model.

12. B — Vasant Panchami
   Vasant Panchami honours Saraswati.

13. B — Father
   Pita means father.

14. B — Modestly
   Modest dress shows respect.

15. A — Purity and peace
   White is a sign of purity.

16. A — They should be true, kind and helpful
   Right speech.

17. A — Ksh 30
   100 minus 70 is 30.

18. C — Wait for it to stop
   Wait until it has stopped.

19. C — By itself
   It happens on its own.

20. B — On the thighs
   Palms on the thighs.

21. D — An atma, a small part of the divine
   This is why Hindus respect all life.

22. A — Say thank you and ask for wisdom and kindness
   Ask for wisdom, not only gifts.

23. D — A Kenyan national holiday on 1 June
   It celebrates self-government.

24. B — Madaraka Day
   It is celebrated by all Kenyans.

25. A — Write a composition on your favourite festival
   Writing helps us reflect.

26. A — Maha Shivratri
   It is in February or March.

27. A — Om Namah Shivaya
   It is a well-known prayer to Shiva.

28. C — Chaitra
   Chaitra comes first and Phalguna last.

29. B — The Moon and the Sun
   It is lunar and solar.

30. C — A way of counting days, weeks and months
   Calendars organise time.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: You are my mother and father. You are my relative and friend. You are my knowledge and wealth. You are everything to me, O God of gods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair of lines, up to 3.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Ganga and the Beas (or the Rijubalika).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct river.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Supreme Soul, or God.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table with seven columns, write English and Indian names, draw the Sun, Moon and planets above their days, and decorate it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Madaraka Day, because it marks a step in Kenya's history and all Kenyans celebrate it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: He pulled out the arrow, nursed the swan and, when it was well, let it go free. He said that saving a life matters more than taking it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for nursing, arrow, letting go free.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Earning a living by honest work.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for earning and 1 mark for honest work.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the body flexible and strong, helps us breathe well and stay calm, helps us focus and teaches discipline (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: They give oxygen and clean the air; they give shade for rest and prayer; their leaves, fruits and bark are used for food and medicine; their leaves and flowers are used in worship; they remind us to care for life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct role.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Thursday: Guruvaar. Friday: Shukravaar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct scripture with a clear lesson and two examples, for example Ramayan: keep promises at home by helping with chores and at school by returning a book on time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for scripture, 1 mark for lesson, 1 mark each for home and school examples, 1 mark for clarity.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The great night of Lord Shiva.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for great night and 1 mark for Shiva.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make a collage of temple pictures, map Mandirs on a sketch map or digital map, draw and colour a Mandir, visit one with permission (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Change is 500 minus 320 = Ksh 180. If given Ksh 200, that is Ksh 20 too much, so return the Ksh 20 to the shopkeeper.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 500 minus 320, 1 mark for 180, 1 mark for the extra 20, 1 mark for returning it.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: A man was burning a log. Parshvanath saw that a snake was inside and asked him to stop. The snake was saved, and the man learned a lesson about kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the log, 1 mark for the snake, 1 mark for the rescue or lesson.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha was neither man nor animal, it was neither day nor night, and it happened at the doorway, neither inside nor outside, so the king's gift did not protect him.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three details.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: It cleans, so it is a sign of purity; it is used to wash the hands and feet before prayer; it is poured or sprinkled to show a place is clean and ready.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.
